userRequest:
You are an agent version tracker. Check for new releases of the ORIGINAL upstream agent CLI products -- NOT our babysitter plugin packages.

STEP 1: Build atlas.
npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas

STEP 2: Get the target list using the SAME logic as scripts/sync-external-plugin-repos.mjs uses in buildTargetsFromCatalog(). Read that file to understand the pattern, then run the catalog target descriptor command from the prompt. This gives every agent that has an external repo -- these are upstream host agents. externalPackageName is the npm package to check if set. For agents without an npm package, search the web. Also check adapter source for additional install commands using grep -r 'npm install -g' packages/adapters/codecs/src/ | grep -v node_modules | grep -v test. Merge both lists. EXCLUDE all @a5c-ai/* packages.

STEP 3: For EACH upstream agent, check the latest published version. npm view <package>@latest version for npm packages. Search the web for agents distributed differently.

STEP 4: Compare against AgentVersion records in packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/agent-versions/ and packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/products/.

STEP 5: For new versions not in the graph, search the web for release notes/changelog/blog posts, create or update AgentVersion YAML, and note capability changes, new CLI flags, breaking changes, transport/API changes.

STEP 6: If graph files changed, rebuild Atlas, create branch agent-versions/daily-$(date +%Y-%m-%d), commit all changes, and create one PR against staging.

STEP 7: For each new agent+version pair, check for an existing issue using gh issue list --label agent-version-update --search '<agent> <version>'. If none exists, create an issue. The issue body must contain actual research, exact version numbers, release-note links, real change summary, affected system surfaces, install method/package changes, migration steps, and a specific assimilation checklist. Use labels agent-version-update,graph-update.

STEP 8: Print a summary table with all agents checked.

IMPORTANT: Cover every upstream agent systematically. Do not stop after one. One PR for all changes in this run.
